claims.claim: Keratella cochlearis at 20 °C: zero-growth food 0.03 mg C/L and r_max 0.28 /d
claims.note: Full text not read. The secondary source (Ramos-Rodríguez et al. 2020, p. 10 of its PDF, Discussion) says Stemberger & Gilbert (1985) reported rmax 0.28 d⁻¹ and a threshold food level of 0.03 mg C/L for K. cochlearis at 20 °C fed Rhodomonas minuta, the latter 'assuming 50% carbon content of food algae by dry mass'. So the mg C value is Ramos-Rodríguez's conversion (50 % C of dry mass), not a number Stemberger & Gilbert printed. The paper's table already says 'via Ramos-Rodríguez et al. 2020'; the code comment (config.js:1512) credits Stemberger & Gilbert directly and should add 'as converted by Ramos-Rodríguez et al. 2020'.

notes: For the human: the JSTOR or Wiley page of doi:10.2307/1939167 opens with a library login. What to check there: the threshold food level and r (or rmax) for K. cochlearis at 20 °C on Rhodomonas minuta, and the units the threshold is printed in (dry mass or cells per mL), so the 0.03 mg C/L conversion can be redone. The secondary source also notes K. cochlearis has among the lowest threshold food levels of the eight species (Stemberger & Gilbert 1987, another paper).
